hook: SCP-1155 is a piece of street art showing an owl-headed humanoid with clawed hands, and it attacks anyone who gets close while nobody else is watching. Containing it is mostly a game of hide and seek across a city. The attacks are described in explicit anatomical detail, including removal of the eyes, tongue, hands, feet and internal organs.
whyItMatters: It combines two familiar rules, a lure you can't stop looking at and a predator that only strikes unseen, and sets them against each other: watching saves a victim but also pushes the image to move. That leaves the Foundation with no clean option, and much of the file is a record of procedures being revised after each bad call. The closing note from a frustrated doctor makes the cost-benefit math explicit.
thingsToNotice: Interrupted attacks reveal a fixed order of mutilation, and one blinded survivor claims he can still see, describing a larder of earlier victims; he later vanishes into a dead-end alley. The other survivor draws the image after him across the city, onto walls, billboards and bridges along the transport route, until command decides to place him in front of it at the city limits to end the hunt. Covering it with a vending machine sends it to a children's playground, and the current site required buying and closing an entire shopping centre, which has given the longest stretch yet without a relocation. The article closes with a doctor arguing that losing a few urban explorers every couple of years is better than covering it at all.
